name: Peer-to-peer rental index: consumer GeForce (4090 / 3090 / 5090 per-GPU-hour)
region: global (16-17 host countries observed per SKU)
price_basis: USD per GPU-HOUR for the GPU component, verified peer-to-peer hosts, 1-GPU bundles, observed 2026-10-03. Asking rental rate, NOT a realised rental. GeForce cards, not datacenter parts - kept as a separate record so consumer and datacenter bands never mix.
notes: OBSERVATION DATE 2026-10-03. Source sup-price-vast-rental-api. THREE DISTINCT BANDS, all observed 2026-10-03, all per-GPU-hour on 1-GPU verified hosts: RTX 4090 n=43, range $0.3024-$0.9356, median $0.4289; RTX 5090 n=41, range $0.4015-$0.7356, median $0.4896; RTX 3090 n=32, range $0.1213-$0.2523, median $0.1498. price_usd records the RTX 4090 median only because the schema has one price slot and 4090 has both the largest sample (n=43) and the tightest spread; the other two medians are carried in notes. THE SEGMENT BOUNDARY, stated as a number: the RTX 3090 rents at ~0.35x the RTX 4090 rate ($0.1498/$0.4289 = 0.35) while its asking PURCHASE price is ~0.46x ($1,514/$3,299 medians, sup-price-picclick-ebay-asking). Rental and purchase price do not move together across these SKUs, which is the practical reason neither number can stand in for the other. Sample sizes here (32-43 per SKU) are large enough that these medians are the most statistically solid figures in this entire slice.
